plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates how individual neurons in a shallow neural network define hyperplane decision boundaries in input spaces of increasing dimension, across three side-by-side panels labeled a), b), and c). Panel a) shows a one-dimensional input space with a horizontal number line labeled x_1 and a single point (the origin dot) marking where the linear threshold function crosses zero, representing a hyperplane as a point in 1D. Panel b) shows a two-dimensional input space with axes x_1 and x_2 and two colored lines passing through the origin: a vertical teal line and a horizontal orange-terracotta line, each representing a separate hyperplane boundary that divides the 2D plane into two half-spaces. Panel c) shows a three-dimensional input space with axes x_1, x_2, and x_3, rendered as a perspective cube with a light gray front face and teal side face, where the flat face of the cube represents a plane slicing through 3D space — the hyperplane in 3D. The figure demonstrates how the linear pre-activation of a neuron defines a hyperplane that separates input space into two regions, with the dimensionality of the hyperplane being one less than the input dimensionality.

elements: panel a: horizontal x1 number line with arrowheads both directions, origin dot, short vertical teal tick crossing the line at the origin
panel b: horizontal orange x1 axis line and vertical teal x2 axis line crossing at the origin dot
panel c: three axes through the origin — x1 horizontal (black arrow), x2 vertical (black arrow), x3 diagonal down-left (black arrow, dashed where hidden)
teal hyperplane containing the x2 axis (the x2-x3 plane), semi-transparent
orange-terracotta hyperplane containing the x1 axis (the x1-x3 plane), semi-transparent
gray reference slab representing the third coordinate plane (x1-x2 plane)
draggable input point P with coordinate drop-lines to the axes
readout label showing sign of each neuron's pre-activation and the combined output class

interactions.label: Input dimension
interactions.teaches: The same neuron equation defines a hyperplane whose dimension is one less than the input space: a point in 1D, a line in 2D, a plane in 3D

interactions.label: Weight w (selected hyperplane)
interactions.teaches: Adjusting one weight component rotates the neuron's hyperplane about the origin, showing that weights encode the orientation of the decision boundary
Moving the input point across each hyperplane flips the sign of that neuron's pre-activation; the combined side-of-plane decisions determine the output class
Rotating the 3D panel reveals that the flat shaded face is a genuine 2D plane slicing the 3D input space, not a solid

demo_steps.title: A hyperplane in 1D
demo_steps.narration: In a one-dimensional input space the 'hyperplane' is just a point — the threshold where the neuron's pre-activation crosses zero.

demo_steps.title: Hyperplanes in 2D
demo_steps.narration: In 2D each neuron defines a line through the origin. The teal and orange lines split the plane into positive and negative half-spaces.

demo_steps.title: Planes in 3D
demo_steps.narration: In 3D each neuron defines a flat plane. Drag the input point across a plane and watch its classification sign flip.

demo_steps.title: Tilt the plane
demo_steps.narration: Change the weight w — the selected plane rotates, and points that were on one side may now fall on the other. Weights set orientation; the point's class follows.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Three mutually exclusive panels. Panel a: x1 line spans ±4 world units, origin dot r≈0.08 at center, teal tick ±0.4 tall at origin. Panel b: axes span ±4 in x1 (orange #d97b4f) and x2 (teal #7fcfc4), front-on 2D view. Panel c: axes span ±3.5; x1 to screen-right, x2 screen-up, x3 down-left diagonal at ~30° below horizontal (dashed on the far side of the origin, as in the source). Teal plane = the plane containing x2 and x3, ~5×5 units, teal #7fcfc4 at 0.45 opacity. Orange plane = plane containing x1 and x3, orange #d97b4f at 0.45 opacity. Gray plane = x1-x2 coordinate plane, light gray #c8c8c8 at 0.35 opacity, drawn slightly larger. Selected (teal) plane rotates about the x2 axis as w varies: normal n = (1, 0, w). Origin dot black. Draggable point P starts at (1.5, 1.0, 1.0), rendered as a black sphere r0.12 with thin dashed drop-lines to each axis. Sign readouts: s_teal = sign(x1 + w·x3), s_orange = sign(x2), combined class shown as text (e.g. region (++)). Panel labels 'a)', 'b)', 'c)' at top-left of each view.
interactionPlan.notes: Implement panels as three scene groups shown/hidden by the toggle — never recreated. Panels a and b should render front-on (override camera to elevation 90/top-down equivalent or azimuth 90, elevation 0 for panel b; treat them as flat 2D). In panel c constrain dragging of P to a movable plane parallel to the view, updating the sign readouts every frame. Recolor the half-space on the positive side of each plane slightly more saturated so region updates are visible when w changes. Use double-sided planes with polygonOffset to avoid z-fighting where planes intersect.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates how individual neurons in a shallow neural network define hyperplane decision boundaries in input spaces of increasing dimension, across three side-by-side panels labeled a), b), and c). Panel a) shows a one-dimensional input space with a horizontal number line labeled x_1 and a single point (the origin dot) marking where the linear threshold function crosses zero, representing a hyperplane as a point in 1D. Panel b) shows a two-dimensional input space with axes x_1 and x_2 and two colored lines passing through the origin: a vertical teal line and a horizontal orange-terracotta line, each representing a separate hyperplane boundary that divides the 2D plane into two half-spaces. Panel c) shows a three-dimensional input space with axes x_1, x_2, and x_3, rendered as a perspective cube with a light gray front face and teal side face, where the flat face of the cube represents a plane slicing through 3D space — the hyperplane in 3D. The figure demonstrates how the linear pre-activation of a neuron defines a hyperplane that separates input space into two regions, with the dimensionality of the hyperplane being one less than the input dimensionality.
